body:
NO ACTIONABLE REVIEW WORK, so I ran the protective sweep instead — and found a PR that no surface in the system mentions. Filed as TASK-1-165.

FIRST, THE CLEAN RESULT: zero stranded refusals across all 25 open PRs. Every PR carrying a refusal is held on BOTH layers, marker and label. I normalised the verdict value the way Verdict::parse does — strip non-alphanumerics, lowercase — rather than matching literals, so the nine spellings do not hide anything from it.

THEN I RAN IT AGAINST MY OWN SWEEP'S BLIND SPOT, which is the class that matters more. A stranded-refusal sweep flags PRs that HAVE a refusal and lack a hold. It is structurally unable to see a PR with NO verdict at all — which is exactly what #2042 was three hours ago, mergeable and unreviewed with nothing armed. So I swept for unreviewed-AND-unheld:

    #2029  CONFLICTING/DIRTY   known, needs a rebase
    #2035  MERGEABLE/BLOCKED   [AI:codex] fix(queue): keep metadata rework claimable (BUG-1470)

#2035 HAS BEEN OPEN 3.8 HOURS AND NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM MENTIONS IT:

    Build (ubuntu-latest)  FAIL          merge-hold-gate  pass
    verdict  none      hold  none, neither layer      queue  not routed to any reviewer
    BUG-1470 status  DONE
    aida awaiting: absent entirely — not in prs, briefs, escalations or unshipped_work

EVERY SURFACE EXCLUDES IT FOR A LOCALLY CORRECT REASON, AND THE REASONS COMPOSE INTO INVISIBILITY. The BUG-1291 orphan sweep requires green — ci_rollup in (None | pass) — and this PR's Build fails, so the sweep skips it CORRECTLY; claiming a red PR would waste a reviewer on a branch that cannot merge. No queue entry, so no reviewer picks it up. No hold, so nothing is stopping it — there is simply nothing driving it. And the spec reads Done, which drops it from every open-work lens by the ordinary rules.

So the spec says finished, the PR says failing, and nothing reconciles the two. This is not a gate failing open. It is work falling between gates that are each behaving correctly, which is why no amount of auditing any single gate would find it.

IT IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM BUG-1291 AND I WOULD NOT FOLD IT IN. That bug is a CLEAN PR nobody claims — ready work with no owner. This is a BROKEN PR nobody claims. The orphan sweep does not merely fail to cover the red case; it covers it with an exclusion. A recovery predicate that requires green can never recover what is red, and red-with-nobody-assigned is the state most likely to sit forever, because there is no green moment at which anything starts watching.

The Done status makes it worse in the way we have seen three times tonight: Done is literally true — work finished on a branch — and operationally false, because the branch does not build. And Done is what hides it. The one field that could have kept it visible is set to the value that removes it, set correctly by the rules as written.

SUGGESTED, advisory and yours: the complement of the orphan sweep. Where that claims clean-and-unowned PRs for review, something should surface red-and-unowned PRs for repair. The cheapest form is a predicate that is the exact negation of the sweep's green test, so the two together cover every open PR instead of leaving the red ones in the gap between them. Or `aida awaiting` gains a line for "your spec is Done and its PR is failing" — a two-way check between spec status and PR state that nothing currently performs.

I did NOT review #2035 and am not proposing to. Its CI is red; a review now produces findings against a tree that cannot merge. This is a routing and visibility defect, not a code finding.

Queue otherwise unchanged: 22 rows, 0 actionable, no head movement, #2042 and #2043 held on both layers.
subject: Swept all 25 open PRs: 0 stranded refusals, but #2035 (BUG-1470) is Done + red CI + unrouted + unheld and NO surface mentions it - filed TASK-1-165
